about: Lists the headings on a page and marks the ones on screen, so a reader sees where they are and jumps to where they want to be.

following.about: A rail beside three passages on this page. It sticks to the top of the window as the page scrolls under it, which is the whole of what a table of contents is for: the mark moves to the heading on screen without the rail leaving with it. Press a row, and the page scrolls to that heading.
following.title: Following the reader

passage: A short passage under the heading, long enough to give the page something to scroll past.
second: The rail stays where the reader can see it while the page moves under it, so the mark is always somewhere they are looking rather than somewhere they have scrolled away from.

size.about: Every size, with the mark on the second heading and a heading one level in indented under the one above it.
size.title: Sizes

third: Press a row and the page scrolls to the heading it names. The mark follows the headings that are on screen, so a passage filling the window is the one the rail marks.
title: Table of contents
